newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev falls as c.bank counters rise.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev falls as c.bank counters rise.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev eased to 1,480-1,490 per dollar at close from the opening's 1,430-1,440 as the central bank was seen countering a lev rise caused by higher dollar supply, dealers said.

"It was dollar bidding by the central bank and some final clients that pressured the lev by some 50 (levs per dollar) from the morning," a commercial bank dealer said. Central bank officials were not available for comment.

The lev opened firmer from Thursday's close of 1,435-1,445 as dollar supply ran high amid low demand from banks and clients and could have neared 1,400 if the central bank had not countered the rise, traders said.
Traders attributed the lev fall partly to the longer value date of spot deals, which falls on May 5. Markets will be closed in Bulgaria from Monday through Thursday for Eastern Orthodox Easter.

The large spread between interest rates on dollar- and lev-denominated investments leaves room for a daily lev drop of some three levs per dollar under current exchange rates and a new, lower main interest rate.
The central bank on Thursday cut its main interest rate to 6.20 percent monthly, effective from Monday, from 8.03 percent now.

According to traders the rate cut was not seen as a reason for the lev slide today because the interest rate spread was still large enough in favour of the lev. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
